Jenna Dewan Faced Criticism, a Partner Suspension, and a Shock Dancing with the Stars Exit. She’s Still Proud.

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2161 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that dancing with the Stars fans let out a collective gasp Tuesday night.
  • Sources indicate that “I had a great time, and I loved getting to share that with the world,” she noted, moments after being eliminated.
  • Not even 48 hours later, Jenna sat down with Women’s Health to share her story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that dancing with the Stars fans let out a collective gasp Tuesday night. Jenna Dewan and her partner, Val Chmerkovskiy, had earned one of the night’s top scores: 28 out of 30. They also won their dance-off against Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, tying for second on the leaderboard with Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov. Then host Alfonso Ribeiro called Dewan’s name, eliminating her from competition.

Sources indicate that “I had a great time, and I loved getting to share that with the world,” she noted, moments after being eliminated. “All love.”.

Not even 48 hours later, Jenna sat down with Women’s Health to share her story.

Jenna Dewan: Overall, it’s really been the saying, “Two things can be true at once.” There's so many different emotions, and it's kind of hard to even put into words because obviously doing a show like this is such an enormous undertaking, and it's physically, emotionally, mentally, spiritually intense. And so, when that's just finished, it's like a light switch goes off, and then you almost don't even know where you are.

I feel all kinds of things. I feel mostly proud. I feel really proud of myself, and I feel proud of the last dance we gave on the ballroom floor, and I feel obviously sad that it's over, that I don't get to give any more dances out there and create any more special pieces. So I think it's really both. I feel really proud of us, and I feel fulfilled, and I feel filled up, and I also feel sad that the journey of creating dances is over.

Recent findings suggest that JD: When you are going through the show, it feels like any week could be you. The show is not necessarily a show about dance. It's not necessarily a competition about the best dancer. It's not about the best dance you give. It's so many other elements that go into it, which is great on a reality show front-end. It makes people tune in for all different kinds of reasons, but in doing that, you never know how it's going to go.

Once it started whittling down, it was the two of us. You kind of come to a place of like, “Okay, this could be our moment.” And I had a feeling—it was a tough week as far as some of the online noise, I would say, that goes with doing the show. So it definitely wasn't out of my mind that it could be a possibility.

Industry observers note that even before Jenna stepped onto the DWTS dance floor, viewers debated whether she belonged in the competition. How much prior dance experience a celebrity contestant can have—while still being considered a fair competitor—has long been a point of debate among viewers.

In a recent development, jenna started her career as a dancer, where she toured alongside legendary performers, including Janet Jackson (she appeared in two music videos of the singer’s). In 2006, she landed her breakout role in Step Up, in which she played a classically trained ballerina. She was the host for television shows World of Dance and Flirty Dancing as well as a judge on Come Dance with Me. Many fans of DWTS cited Jenna’s impressive resume as an unfair advantage. “How is Jenna Dewan part of this? She was a professional dancer. Hello! So unfair already,” one X user wrote on the platform after the official season 35 cast announcement.

Sources indicate that it should be noted, however, Jenna is not the first celebrity to join the show with previous dance experience—and it’s safe to say she’ll be far from the last. Stars like Heather Morris, Jordan Fisher, and Charli D’Amelio have all undergone criticism for joining the show in the past, despite having a substantial leg up among fellow contestants. Even Alfonso, the show’s current host and season 19 winner, had prior dance experience.

JD: I will say, through the history of watching the show and what I know about the show, is I've seen there be an problem with people with dance backgrounds, and that obviously there's a lot of opinions on whether we should even have people compete on the show that have dance backgrounds.

I definitely asked quite a few times, “Are you sure you guys want me on the show?” But the incredible people who do the show were really confident in expressing to me that this show had changed a lot, and that it’s not Dancing with the Stars Who Have Never Danced. They wanted a very dynamic cast with all different levels and strengths they bring to the ballroom. I knew it would be an uphill battle for me for sure, just from the patterns of the show and the loyalists of the show and how they feel. But ultimately, the gift of doing something just for myself was really intoxicating, and it won over any sort of doubts or hesitations I had.

JD: The hardest part of the show, I would say, is it really teaches you that joy and difficulty can exist together. There were so many highs of this journey, and then so many moments of frustration and negative noise and criticism that is honestly sad, because it tries to suck out the joy from the experience.

Even for myself with a dance background, it is vulnerable to put yourself out there in the ballroom every Tuesday and be like, “Hey guys, watch my dance and tell me what you think.” And then you have the whole other element of this social, online, noisy world that is almost like they're looking to tear people down, and I felt that that was an unfortunate shade to this show that didn't need to happen.

Recent findings suggest that JD: Part of the journey of the show is interesting because for the first good couple weeks, you rarely see any of the other contestants, because you are really in your own rehearsal space, and you're just trying to get the dances down as fast as you can with your partner. I think it was rare seeing people in the hallways and connecting with some of the contestants. But yeah, we definitely would talk.

I think at one point Connor [Wood] made me laugh so hard because he mentioned he had seen some of the online social negativity, and he said, “Everyone needs to go back to journaling.” I laughed so hard, because he is exactly right. At some point, we all thought it was okay to just get online and to be mean for no reason. We are real human beings that see this and feel this, and I think that that gets forgotten.

In a recent development, when we did the team dance, that was when we really were able to start bonding as the contestants, because we were finally together working towards one dance and in a room together. I absolutely love them, and we were all definitely talking about this and sharing our experiences with this, and how most of us at that point, I think, had taken it off our phone or turned off social media.

It has been revealed that JD: Naturally, because of my dance background, there were really high expectations that I put on myself, and that the world was putting on me. I didn't even realize it was happening, but it was creating this feeling that I needed to let go of perfection and kind of just get comfortable being seen and just being there. I didn't need to prove anything.

According to recent reports, I think I just realized how much of my life I spent wanting to get things right. And this experience really challenged me in that way, because what I realized is, you just can't grow if you're constantly worried about being perfect. I had to learn to be a little uncomfortable, to be critiqued again, to make some mistakes, to be vulnerable, and just let people see me in the middle of figuring something out. There's actually a lot of freedom in that, because I didn't have ballroom dance down perfectly by the time I got out there.

JD: I thought that every dance we did. I thought that during the week two jive, and it was intriguing to me that [the judges] were so critical of certain dances. However, when I look back, there was a lot of growth for me.

There was a whole element of this that was sort of discovering my strength in a fresh way because I have had three children, I've navigated huge life transitions, I've built a career, a family, a life, And now, I'm stepping into this show where I'm pushing myself physically, emotionally, creatively in a way that I haven't in years. So I think I just surprised myself with how strong I am, and not just physically, but emotionally.

According to recent reports, jenna also faced an unexpected complication when her partner, Val, was suspended for one episode of the show following a social media post he made about DWTS judge Carrie Ann Inaba. After Carrie Ann criticized his wife, fellow pro dancer Jenna Johnson, for including what she considered an illegal lift in her routine with Harry Shum Jr., Val posted, “You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night.” The now-deleted post was widely interpreted as a reference to the 2022 Academy Awards, when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock after making a joke about his wife, Jada Pinkett Smith.

Carrie Ann appeared to interpret the post as a threat. She shared a screenshot of a Page Six story about it on Instagram, writing, “So this is what we are doing now?”.

Industry observers note that on Oct. 17, DWTS production company BBC Studios said Val would not participate in the Oct. 20 episode. Jenna danced with pro Alan Bersten in his place.

JD: I said this, and I really mean this, that I did not foresee having as many challenges as I did that were thrown at me during my Dancing with the Stars journey. However, the challenges of it gave me an opportunity to walk my talk, and I always think that when that happens, you can go back to your true north, to what’s your intention for doing something. How do you want to show up as a human when you’re experiencing challenges? And I kept going back to my kids. When the mid-season suspension happened, and all these things were going on, I thought, “I have a real opportunity here. I can be annoyed and bitter and upset about this, or I can show up with grace and love and joy and focus on the moment.”.

That particular week was about my mom and my dedication to her. And she was in town, thrilled to have this dance with me, and thrilled to experience this moment. And I thought that this is something she's going to remember. We're all going to remember my family forever. Let's focus on that, and let's not worry about all of this that's going on.

According to recent reports, JD: I’ve seen that, and I feel like with just life in general, even outside of Dancing with the Stars, that is absolutely something that most females have experienced. I think there's been a great change in our world, but I think for years upon years upon years, women have had a fight against misogyny and inherent bias. Women at times in life are just held to a different standard than men, and I think that that is a real reflection.

We're expected to be exceptional, but also humble and confident, but not too confident, skilled, but not struggling enough to earn praise. There's all this pressure on women. It feels like sometimes if a woman is strong or capable, the expectations become that much higher. I think people are so busy expecting women to be extraordinary that we forget to celebrate them for being extraordinary.

According to recent reports, JD: It's never too late for a new chapter in life. And I think if there was like, one thing I wanted people to take away from my whole journey, it’s that we're never finished becoming who we are, and it's never too late to choose your own passion in life and your own joy in life. There isn't some age where you stop growing and dreaming and trying new things.

Alyssa Cruz is the social media editor at Women’s Health, where she drives social strategy and helps shape the brand’s voice across platforms. Prior to WH, she worked at CBS News and palabra. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is sending out a hopeful message to the crypto space in the wake of a brutal market crash that is causing ADA to come very close to falling out of the top 20 crypto assets.

Recently, Hoskinson took to X to respond to a frustrated Cardano fan who posted a screenshot showing ADA falling almost 10% in the last 24 hours.

In a recent development, “It’s all going to be ok,” remarked Hoskinson. “Everyone will be happy next year after all this madness, hate and idiocy.”.

The recent crypto market crash has proven to be extremely brutal for a lot of different assets, and Cardano is certainly one of the worst affected.

In recent trading, ADA has fallen all the way down to around $0.15.

At these levels, ADA is currently down around 95% from its all-time high of $3.09, which was reached in September 2021, based on data from CoinGecko.

This represents an almost complete loss of investment value for those who bought at the all-time high.

Overall, Cardano is also down around 35% in the last month and almost 60% since the start of 2026.

As a result, Cardano’s market cap has fallen all the way down to around $5.7 billion, with ADA dropping to 18th place in CoinGecko’s crypto rankings.

This is a very precarious position for the once-dominant altcoin Cardano, which is now extremely close to falling out of the top 20.

It seems as though there are a few different factors at play behind Cardano’s poor performance.

It has been revealed that first of all, there has been a huge sell-off in the broader crypto market. Bitcoin has seen major drops, leading to more selling pressure on major altcoins.

This decline has coincided with a falling technology stock market, ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty, outflows from crypto investment products, and mass liquidations of leveraged positions.

That said, there are clearly some issues with Cardano beyond the wider market struggles.

For one, Cardano has faced a lot of criticism over the years for the blockchain’s relatively low adoption, even after years of development. This is especially evident when compared to other chains like Ethereum and Solana.

In fact, Cardano’s decentralized finance ecosystem has recently seen around $46 million in total value locked, as reported by DefiLlama.

Elsewhere, Hoskinson recently found himself embroiled in another controversy surrounding Cardano’s future.

In another recent X post, Hoskinson lashed out at certain commentators who keep bashing the blockchain for its apparent lack of adoption.

He noted that critics initially claimed Cardano suffered from poor on-chain metrics, few real-world use cases and technology that no one wanted to use.

Then, when Hoskinson decided to work on developing apps that would be able to attract millions of people and billions in assets, it seemed as though those same critics began claiming he was scamming everyone.

“You people are both stupid and scum. I can’t fix stupid,” noted Hoskinson. “Grow up.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as Bitcoin hurtles toward the $60k support level, critics are having a field day once again, calling it a scam and a pyramid scheme, among other things. However, one analyst noted that the digital currency has fallen every 4 years or so over the last 3 cycles, and the digital asset is simply following established trends.

Industry observers note that the post documents that every major price drop has been met with triumphant celebrations over the digital currency’s demise. BTC has already dropped 50% from its all-time high (ATH) of $126.5k set roughly a year ago. While naysayers are having a field day right now, seasoned investors understand that the premier digital currency has a history of recovering well in the years that follow.

Bitcoin first experienced a major crash in 2011 when it dropped to $2. It was the first time it happened on such a noticeable scale, and many legacy analysts quickly declared it “dead” or a scam. However, Bitcoin recovered well and experienced a major bull run two years later that propelled it above $1,000 for a short while. This represented a 500x price increase.

Afterward, Bitcoin started to cool off again, and in 2015, the premier digital asset crashed to $250, sparking another episode of critics calling it a scam. However, the digital asset once again started to rise strongly two years after this occurrence and reached as high as $19,500 in late 2017, representing a 78x increase.

However, 2018 proved brutal for the cryptocurrency, and it dropped to sub-$3,000 levels near the end of the calendar year. Once again, the naysayers, led by Peter Schiff, were quick to declare it dead. The cryptocurrency remained on the defensive for about a year before beginning a major price recovery. By the end of 2021, Bitcoin had risen to $69k, representing a 23x price increase.

In a recent development, the 2022 bear market, like clockwork, soon followed, and the digital asset dropped to $15k, once again triggering critics. However, the bearish scenario eventually ended, and Bitcoin started to recover strongly in early 2024, resulting in a major price boom that pushed the cryptocurrency to $126.5k by October 2025, representing an 8.4x gain. Now, the digital currency is struggling above $60k and may likely fall even further below the key support. Critics are active, and in all practical purposes, this is peak FUD season.

Bitcoin’s recent troubles align with previous cycles, and it is important for long-term investors to stay patient and avoid panic selling.

Enjin Matrixchain Votes on OpenGov Today: What Changes for ENJ Holders on November 16

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16.
  • Enjin's newly introduced proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ.
  • According to recent reports, enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Recent findings suggest that enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16. Here is how the nine tracks, the 1,000 ENJ deposit and conviction voting work, and what the Relaychain vote shows.

Enjin's newly introduced proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ. It's actually the cheap part.

According to recent reports, enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release. The referendum opened November 10. If it passes, the upgrade is targeted for November 16 at block #12,319,600, with the network moving from runtime 1.3.1 to 1.4.3. Enjin's Fort Canning announcement lays out the plan, and the official changelog carries the technical detail.

The Relaychain has already made the jump. Referendum #16 approved its upgrade on October 28, and it went live on November 9. The Matrixchain vote is the second half of one upgrade, and it is the half that changes how Matrixchain makes decisions from then on.

Early coverage reported the schedule and the headline numbers: nine tracks, 1,000 ENJ. The changelog and the governance portal show the mechanics behind them, and those mechanics change more than the headlines suggest.

According to recent reports, today, the Matrixchain runs its governance through the older Democracy, Council and Technical Committee pallets, the modules that handle proposals and votes. Fort Canning replaces all three with a newly introduced set: Referenda, Conviction Voting, Origins, Whitelist and the Enjin Fellowship. Under OpenGov, any account can submit a referendum on one of nine tracks, and from the moment the upgrade lands, Matrixchain's own upgrades go through that process.

A track is a lane for a particular kind of decision. Enjin's changelog describes the families: Root and the admin tracks for the highest-stakes changes, Whitelisted Caller for proposals the Fellowship fast-tracks, and two special tracks, Referendum Killer and Referendum Canceller, for stopping a proposal that shouldn't proceed. Matrixchain gets no treasury tracks: those, sized by how much a proposal would spend, stay on the Relaychain, where treasury requests now go. Each track has its own deposit, approval curve and enactment period, and the Enjin Fellowship can fast-track time-sensitive proposals.

In a recent development, splitting decisions this way means a small treasury request doesn't face the same bar as a change to the chain's core. Riskier tracks demand larger deposits and more support, while smaller ones move faster and cost less.

In a recent development, the submission deposit rises from 0.025 ENJ to 1,000 ENJ on every track, a 40,000-fold increase. The deposit is refunded when a referendum passes or is canceled, and it exists to deter spam. As an illustration, using the roughly $66 million market cap reported in early October, ENJ traded near three cents, which would put 1,000 ENJ around $33.

Sources indicate that that is only the entry ticket. The cost that matters comes next. A referendum also needs a decision deposit before it moves into voting, and the changelog lists steep figures: 2,500,000 ENJ on Root and Fellowship Admin, 1,000,000 ENJ on the other admin tracks, and 2,500 to 250,000 ENJ on the Relaychain's treasury tracks. At the same illustrative price, the 2.5 million ENJ Root deposit comes to roughly $80,000, about 0.12% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance.

So proposing is cheap, and pushing a proposal through is not. Anyone can raise an idea, but anyone who wants the network to vote on something big needs real stake in the outcome. The changelog says the same values apply on both chains, and Matrixchain adopts them for its new tracks.

The best evidence of how these votes work comes from the Relaychain referendum that has already finished. Enjin's governance portal indicates referendum #16 as finalised, approved on October 28 and enacted on November 9.

In a recent development, the final tally on the page is small. Eleven voters cast 381,303.02 ENJ of conviction-weighted voting power, and all of it went to Aye: 100% in favor, 0 ENJ against. The page also demonstrates raw, unweighted support of 271,303.2 ENJ, which it describes as the total balance backing the proposal and the figure the support curve uses. The conviction multiplier on the page runs from under 1x up to 6x.

According to recent reports, two numbers stand out. First, an entire chain upgrade passed with 271,303 ENJ of raw support, about 0.013% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance, a figure worked out from the portal's number. Second, conviction added about 110,000 ENJ of weight on top of the raw balance, an average multiplier of roughly 1.4x. Voters picked up some extra weight, but most didn't lock their tokens for the long periods that earn the top multipliers.

According to recent reports, A 100% Aye result notes little by itself. A scheduled upgrade with no organized opposition passes easily, and the tally shows how thin engagement was.

Fort Canning adds the safeguard that thin turnout calls for. A referendum now needs a minimum share of total ENJ voting in support. The changelog sets 0.5% on Root and the admin tracks, 0.005% to 0.125% on the Relaychain's treasury tracks, 0.1% for Referendum Killer and 0.05% for Referendum Canceller. Measured against 2.02 billion ENJ, that means about 10.1 million ENJ on Root, roughly 101,000 to 2.5 million on the treasury tracks, about 2.02 million to kill a referendum and about 1.01 million to cancel one.

Referendum #16's 271,303 ENJ of raw support would clear the lowest treasury floor of about 101,000 ENJ, but it would miss the Root floor by a factor of about 37. The page doesn't show which track the referendum used, and a runtime upgrade typically sits on a high-stakes track, so the Root comparison works as an illustration and not as a finding. The floors also didn't exist when #16 passed, since Fort Canning introduced them.

In a recent development, that is the real change. Under the upcoming rules, 11 wallets can't carry a chain-level decision on their own. Low turnout means failure, and proposals that matter will need far more ENJ behind them. Enjin's changelog claims Matrixchain upgrades go through OpenGov starting with this one, which suggests today's vote still runs on the current system, so the floors will first bite on the first OpenGov referendum.

Holders who haven't voted can still do so through Enjin's governance portal before the window closes. Voting locks tokens, so the lock length is worth checking first. Enjin's support article on voting explains the trade-off: the longer the lock, the more a vote counts, and tokens stay locked until the period ends.

In a recent development, node operators on the Matrixchain can wait for the result before upgrading, as Enjin has indicated, and then follow the changelog for the version to install. Relaychain operators already needed client version 1.8.1.

This vote is more about control than speed. OpenGov spreads decisions across tracks with deposits and support floors built for the weight of each choice, and it moves ENJ holders from voting on a handful of items to a standing governance system. The Relaychain's first vote showed how little participation it took under the old rules, and the first referenda after November 16 will show whether holders turn out for the latest ones. If most proposals stall at the decision deposit, the system costs too much. If they clear with a handful of voters, the floors aren't doing their job. Either result will tell holders what their ENJ can do.

Despite the market downturn, XRP Ledger is showing a somewhat reassuring trend: the price has bounced toward the $1 mark and, thankfully, the move is followed by a volume uptick, which could start a proper recovery rally.

XRP is trading at $0.96 after dipping to $0.89. The $1 threshold, which essentially enables a rapid decrease if broken, gave in on November 14. It's the first time XRP traded below $1 since mid-August.

It has been revealed that the market is bearish, and the RSI dropped into the 20-ish zone, which is considered "extremely oversold". Moving averages are still rapidly diverging, which might further reinforce the bearish dynamic.

Recent findings suggest that even if XRP reclaims the round number, bulls might still stay sidelined. If bulls somehow wake up, a recovery toward $1.2 is the main priority, as it's the level where a lot of investors accumulated XRP in the past.

On the other hand, the Ledger reveals elevated activity, with the potential to go further and reclaim levels we haven't seen in the bear market. Still, elevated activity during a prolonged market descent is not something we should just shake off.

Sources indicate that according to on-chain data, payment volume on the XRP Ledger reached around 1.1 billion XRP, up 139.9%. Active accounts went up by 154.5%, reaching 42,300. Payments volume growth is substantial, but not record-breaking by any means.

The XRP Ledger has seen substantial growth in various on-chain metrics, which, unfortunately, does not give the price enough support. A lot of the Ledger activity might be automated, driven by either trading bots or sophisticated LLM models. The market is mostly driven by speculative interest rather than fundamental network usage.

The activity of investors who are trying to cash out or pull their holdings away from exchanges could be the key here. Growing payments volume most likely reflects growing fear among investors, as some of them move funds to exchanges in order to liquidate their coins.

Payments volume rises, but so does the bear market pressure, with a possibility of a further downturn that could make things worse than they already are.

According to recent reports, the price of Bitcoin has dropped by around 19% over the 50 days before the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic, and the decline is similar to the one that Bitcoin had ahead of the SpaceX listing in June. At press time, Bitcoin is trading at $65,450, according to TradingView. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Nov. 13, and it dropped below $67,000 over the weekend.

Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, is set to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Nov. 19. The AI tech giant is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each and aims to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO. At the top of the range, Anthropic would be valued at around $1.4 trillion, and the company has also arranged a $26 billion private placement.

According to recent reports, spaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO this summer, so the Anthropic listing is close to it in size. Before the SpaceX IPO, the price of Bitcoin also went down by around 19%.

Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee called the current drawdown a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, as investors sell liquid assets to buy shares in the largest offerings of the year.

According to recent reports, after SpaceX started trading on Nasdaq, the price of Bitcoin kept falling for another 18 days. After that, Bitcoin went up, and 100 days after the IPO, it was 28% above its close on the day of the listing.

If Bitcoin repeats this pattern after the Anthropic IPO, it could reach $90,000 by the end of February 2027, according to Strive CEO Matt Cole.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared the comparison of the two charts on X and called Cole's numbers "an interesting analysis." Still, some owners in the replies under the post blamed the drop of Bitcoin on selling by Binance, not on the IPO calendar.

However, strong financial results may not be enough to satisfy investors. Concerns surrounding AI spending, rising memory costs and leadership uncertainty have increased the pressure on the company. With Nvidia shares facing renewed volatility, can its latest earnings restore confidence in AI stocks, or is Wall Street preparing for another sell-off?

It has been revealed that nvidia faces exceptionally high expectations heading into its latest earnings report. Wall Street analysts expect the manufacturer to generate approximately $108.85 billion in revenue and $2.47 in adjusted earnings per share for fiscal Q3 2027. That would represent revenue growth of roughly 91% from $57.01 billion reported in the same quarter last year.

The manufacturer had previously guided for third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, putting its official forecast broadly in line with analyst expectations. The previous quarter provides a strong benchmark. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in Q2 FY2027 revenue, up 106% year over year, while adjusted earnings reached $2.22 per share. Its Data Center business generated $89 billion, accounting for the overwhelming majority of quarterly revenue.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s Data Center business remains the biggest driver of its valuation, making this segment the most crucial part of the upcoming earnings report. Analyst estimates put fiscal Q3 Data Center revenue at approximately $101.8 billion. Demand for Blackwell GPUs and expanding AI infrastructure investments from cloud providers are expected to support the increase.

Sources indicate that investors will also examine the company’s Vera Rubin platform, which is expected to become an increasingly key contributor to future revenue. Nvidia has remarked that Vera Rubin is entering production, while its earlier guidance indicated that the platform could account for around 20% of Data Center revenue in Q3.

It has been revealed that the bigger question is whether hyperscalers and AI companies will continue spending aggressively on computing capacity. Microsoft, Amazon, Google and other major technology companies remain crucial customers in the AI infrastructure cycle.

It has been revealed that if Nvidia signals that demand remains strong into fiscal 2028, it could support sentiment across the semiconductor sector. Any indication of slower orders or delayed infrastructure spending, however, could pressure not only NVDA but also AMD, Broadcom and other AI-linked stocks.

Nvidia’s earnings call will face another crucial test: whether rising costs and business uncertainty are beginning to affect its growth outlook. The firm previously guided for a non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 74% in fiscal Q3. However, management also warned that higher memory costs could push margins lower in the following quarter, with a projected range of 71%–72% for Q4 FY2027.

According to recent reports, china exposure is another concern investors will monitor. Nvidia’s previous Q3 revenue outlook did not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China, leaving investors to assess how much additional growth could come from other markets.

Recent findings suggest that leadership uncertainty adds another layer to the earnings event. Recent reports surrounding Jensen Huang’s departure and the company’s leadership transition have increased investor concerns ahead of the results. Interim leadership will need to reassure investors about product execution, customer relationships and the company’s long-term strategy.

Recent findings suggest that the earnings call could therefore matter as much as the financial numbers. Investors will be looking for clear answers on future demand, margins and management’s confidence in the AI growth cycle.

Nvidia stock is approaching a decisive earnings test after losing nearly one-third of its value from its October record high. NVDA stock is trading around $159.92 on November 16, down approximately 32% from the October 6 peak of $243.37. The recent decline has brought the stock close to its 52-week low of $148.80.

Recent findings suggest that the earnings reaction will likely determine which direction NVDA takes next. Strong results, upbeat Data Center guidance and confidence from interim CEO Colette Kress could help buyers regain control. However, weaker forward guidance or concerns about AI spending could push shares back toward recent lows.

According to recent reports, according to CoinGlass, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on the Coinbase spot market reached -$1.08 billion between Oct. 31 and Nov. 15. CVD reveals the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

According to recent reports, the price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

Recent findings suggest that the data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some owners on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that demonstrated client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several people in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

According to recent reports, binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

In a recent development, coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

According to recent reports, anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

The CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.

It has been revealed that thirdly, XRP is presently in negative funding at -0.0082%. Negative funding in perpetual futures markets means that short sellers are paying long sellers to keep positions open, a sign traders are bearish on the market.

XRP fell for 10 straight days from November 5 to November 14, 2026. Price lost momentum after losing the daily MA 200 at the close of October. The cryptocurrency lost another crucial support in early October, the daily MA 50, weakening bulls.

Recent findings suggest that stablecoin supply is shrinking fast, dropping $17 billion over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022. As holders swap stablecoins to fiat, they drain buying power from BTC and crypto, analysts at Glassnode mentioned.

It will be watched if buying power returns to the market; according to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a massive buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when.".

The daily RSI has entered oversold levels, with the possibility of a relief rally in the coming session. Such a recovery, if sustained, will target the daily MA 50 and 200 at $1.25 and $1.30. Further downside is expected to find support at $0.77.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lawmakers are instead expected to focus on investigating crypto companies with ties to President Donald Trump.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the crypto industry’s run of friendly treatment in Washington looks set to end. Cody Carbone, chief executive of The Digital Chamber, warned that a Democrat-controlled Congress will be “very hostile” to digital assets. Broad market structure legislation such as the CLARITY Act is now unlikely to pass.

Lawmakers are instead expected to focus on investigating crypto companies with ties to President Donald Trump. The political shift comes as Bitcoin trades at its lowest level since July.

Sources indicate that carbone remarked in an interview that the industry is unlikely to get the broad legislation it had pushed for. The CLARITY Act, meant to set clear rules for how digital assets are regulated in the US, has been left in limbo.

Two longtime critics of the industry are set to gain influence over financial policy: Senator Elizabeth Warren in the Senate and Representative Maxine Waters in the House.

For crypto firms, the agenda in Washington is moving from passing rules to defending against scrutiny.

Trump’s Crypto Ties Move Into the Spotlight.

Sources indicate that the industry is preparing for sweeping inquiries into crypto businesses connected to the President. Carbone expects Warren and Waters to press hard on Trump’s links to digital assets.

The Digital Chamber’s strategy is to counter those investigations by shifting the debate to the technology itself. Carbone wants supportive lawmakers to steer hearings toward topics such as tokenization, so the conversation is about substance rather than politics.

The strategy depends on finding allies inside the incoming majority. Carbone admitted that pro-crypto Democrats are “few and far between,” but noted their numbers are growing.

Many of the newly elected Democrats are young and focused on technology. According to Carbone, several have told the industry they are “crypto curious.”.

According to recent reports, the Digital Chamber looks to target moderates and junior committee members. Carbone stated no single Democrat can take on Warren alone, but a larger group could. The aim is to build enough support within the party to push back against the more hostile voices.

Data Center Backlash Adds Fresh Pressure.

Industry observers note that opposition to data centers poses another major threat, Carbone said. Local resistance to energy-heavy facilities hits both crypto mining and artificial intelligence.

According to recent reports, carbone said voters made their concerns clear in the November election and have a right to be skeptical. Still, the industry argues that bans and moratoriums are the wrong response.

The Digital Chamber plans to show lawmakers how data centers can bring jobs and revenue to struggling districts. Carbone described blockchain, digital assets and AI as closely linked industries, and framed leadership in all three as a matter of national competitiveness.

“100%” Risk of Losing Ground to China.

The big warning was about America’s global position. Asked whether the US could lose its lead in the sector within the next two years, Carbone answered and said “100%.”.

According to recent reports, developers in crypto and AI are already moving to friendlier places such as the UAE and Singapore. Carbone pointed to China, which holds the most blockchain patents worldwide, as the country most likely to take the lead if the US falls behind.

“If we don’t lead, other adversaries will,” Carbone stated, arguing that the US must set the global rules before its rivals do.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana has officially turned a major page in its history, dropping the long-standing ‘beta’ tag after more than six years and adopting protocol version 1.0. The milestone marks a significant step in the network’s evolution as it moves beyond its experimental phase, with ongoing efforts to improve transaction speed, finality, and overall performance. The development could also strengthen Solana’s appeal to developers and institutional players, raising fresh questions about whether SOL is poised for a latest bullish chapter.

Solana has officially retired its six-year-old “mainnet beta” designation, with the network’s foundation saying the rebranding highlights the significant strides made since the blockchain first released in March 2020.

Sources indicate that “Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience,” the Solana foundation wrote in a Monday statement. “That progress continues with this simplification of nomenclature.”.

Industry observers note that the foundation emphasized that Solana has operated as a fully live network since its launch, arguing that retaining the beta designation had become outdated. It noted that the label, traditionally associated with technology still in its early testing stages, no longer accurately represented a blockchain already processing transactions and hosting active applications.

According to the Solana Foundation, the reclassification requires no action from customers. Existing SOL holdings, account balances, and transaction histories will remain unchanged despite the protocol’s transition to version 1.0.

The foundation also advised developers and validator operators to stick to the specific instructions accompanying software releases, stressing that the newly introduced protocol designation does not mean all network upgrades or improvements become active automatically.

In a recent development, solana’s move to protocol version 1.0 comes as the network continues pursuing major infrastructure improvements, with Alpenglow and Firedancer among its most closely watched developments. Both initiatives aim to strengthen Solana’s performance, reliability, and ability to support growing on-chain activity.

The first major milestone is Alpenglow, Solana’s latest consensus protocol, which went live on mainnet on October 21. The upgrade targets transaction finality of approximately 150 milliseconds, a significant improvement from the previous 12.8-second timeframe. Transaction finality refers to the moment a blockchain permanently confirms a transaction, meaning it is considered settled and cannot be reversed under normal network conditions. Faster finality could make Solana more attractive for payments, decentralized finance, and institutional applications that require near-instant transaction settlement.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Firedancer brings another notable improvement through an independently developed validator client built by Jump Crypto. It provides an alternative to Solana’s existing Agave client, reducing the network’s dependence on a single software implementation. This client diversity could strengthen network resilience by limiting the risk that a bug affecting one implementation disrupts the entire blockchain.

The foundation added that the rebranding establishes a unified system for tracking Solana’s updates, allowing developers, validators, and infrastructure providers to identify protocol changes consistently, regardless of the software client they use.

Chandler Fang, founder of AI payments startup t54.ai, has said that the tech giant's x402 Facilitator on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has processed more than 10 million AI agent transactions. Fang made the comments in an interview that the XRPL Foundation published on X on November 15, and the interviewer put the number of these payments at 11.7 million.

According to recent reports, according to Fang, XRPL had almost no transactions made by AI agents three or four months before the interview, which was recorded at XRP Seoul 2026. "The entire volume got ramped up very quickly in the three months," he mentioned.

The x402 Facilitator works as a bridge between AI agents and payments, and agents can use XRP or the RLUSD stablecoin to move money without a separate wallet setup for every agent. Fang stated that more than 200 merchants are already on the network.

According to Fang, the most common use case is paying for AI compute. Instead of paying $20 to $200 a month for an AI subscription, an agent can pay around $1 or 50 cents for a single task. "Instead, they can purchase this single compute for about $1, or 50 cents, and it can be settled on the XRPL," Fang mentioned.

Sources indicate that fang said that such payments have low value and high frequency, so the high throughput and low fees of XRPL give the network an advantage. He also expects agent payments to move into real-life purchases over the next few quarters. "We have the coffee shop right outside our booth, right? And we are trying to empower consumers to use XRP and agent payments to finish a real-life transaction," Fang said.

According to Fang, trust is the main matter for agent payments, and t54.ai's Trustline product focuses on risk management for the financial activity of AI agents. He compared the service with the chargeback feature of credit cards. "So there is no lawsuit. It is a similar experience for agents," Fang mentioned.

According to recent reports, t54.ai is also part of Mastercard's agentic payment program, where the startup is responsible for risk management. The x402 Facilitator processes transactions based on Mastercard Verifiable Intent, a protocol that verifies the behavior of AI agents.

Fang remarked that t54.ai, Ripple and Mastercard are in talks about a three-way collaboration, and the first results will be shown at an upcoming hackathon.

It has been revealed that "The ten million transactions are just a starting point. I think next year you should expect a lot more transactions. Maybe even more transactions settled on XRPL will be done by AI agents than by humans," Fang said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bitcoin staking allows holders to earn rewards on their BTC without selling the underlying asset. In 2026, Stacks, Babylon, Core, Starknet and Stacking DAO offer different approaches, with varying rewards, custody models and staking requirements.

Industry observers note that stacks targets approximately 3% annualized rewards in BTC, while Babylon, Core and Starknet distribute rewards in their native tokens. Stacking DAO offers liquid staking with BTC-linked returns.

Choosing a platform requires looking beyond advertised yields to understand token requirements, custody arrangements and withdrawal conditions.

Rates as of November 10, 2026. Stacks quotes a target annual yield, Babylon quotes APR, and other displayed rates may use different calculation conventions.

The main differences concern reward sources, custody arrangements, additional capital requirements and withdrawal flexibility.

Bitcoin staking rewards vary by source, denomination and additional capital requirements.

Stacks is a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC.

Stacks miners commit BTC through Proof of Transfer (PoX) to compete for the right to produce Stacks blocks and earn STX rewards. The committed BTC is distributed to staking participants, providing the source of their BTC rewards. PoX has distributed over 4,200 BTC since January 2021.

Direct Bitcoin staking targets approximately 3% annualized yield, with weekly BTC rewards. Since September 2026, three staking bonds have sold out, bringing total BTC staked to 1,740 BTC.

Babylon distributes BABY rewards funded by newly issued tokens through the protocol’s inflation mechanism. Its displayed APR ranges from 0.04% to 0.52%, with the higher rate requiring participants to co-stake BABY alongside BTC.

Returns depend on reward distribution and BABY’s value relative to Bitcoin.

Sources indicate that core distributes CORE rewards to participants who delegate BTC to validators securing its blockchain. Rewards come from newly issued CORE block rewards and transaction fees.

Its displayed top-tier yield is 0.79%, with higher reward tiers requiring participants to stake CORE alongside BTC.

Starknet allows holders of supported tokenized Bitcoin assets to delegate them to validators securing the network.

Sources indicate that participants earn newly minted STRK tokens, with a displayed yield of 2.91%. Actual returns depend on network participation and STRK’s value relative to BTC.

Industry observers note that stacking DAO provides liquid Bitcoin staking through stBTC, a token representing an sBTC-based staking position. BTC rewards generated through Bitcoin staking on Stacks accumulate in the position, increasing the amount of sBTC backing each stBTC over time.

Its displayed yield is 2.31%, with rewards accruing automatically rather than requiring separate claims.

Why reward denominations matter.

A 4% annual reward paid in a token that loses 50% of its value against BTC would be worth approximately 2% of the original BTC position, assuming other factors remain unchanged.

BTC rewards avoid this specific reward-token conversion risk, although staking still involves other costs and risks.

Stacks, Babylon and Core support native Bitcoin staking on Bitcoin L1, while Starknet and Stacking DAO use Bitcoin-backed assets on other layers.

In direct self-custodial staking, BTC remains timelocked on Bitcoin L1 under the participant’s custody. Institutions can also access this route through qualified custody infrastructure, including BitGo and Anchorage Digital.

Recent findings suggest that BTC is locked on Bitcoin L1 and delegated to finality providers supporting the Babylon ecosystem. Bitcoin remains native, but the staking position is subject to protocol slashing conditions.

BTC holders timelock their Bitcoin on L1 and delegate staking weight to Core validators without transferring BTC to another chain.

Participants stake supported tokenized Bitcoin assets on Starknet, introducing dependencies on the underlying token’s backing and smart contracts.

Industry observers note that participants can deposit sBTC, a Bitcoin-backed asset on Stacks, or BTC, which is converted into sBTC. In return, they receive stBTC, representing their staking position and accruing BTC rewards. Part of Stacks’ Bitcoin staking capacity is allocated to this pooled staking route. Unlike direct staking on Stacks, this route is not self-custodial.

Native Bitcoin custody avoids certain bridge and wrapper dependencies but does not remove staking-specific risks.

Some protocols require additional token commitments, while others use them to increase rewards.

According to recent reports, stacks uses STX as staking capacity. Direct participants commit STX worth approximately 5% of their BTC position, locked for the staking term.

Babylon offers increased rewards through BABY co-staking, while Core uses CORE dual staking to determine reward tiers.

Starknet does not require participants to pair STRK with their BTC for standard delegation. Stacking DAO handles the underlying STX commitment without requiring participants to provide it separately.

These requirements affect capital efficiency because additional tokens introduce further price exposure.

Withdrawal conditions vary across staking models.

Sources indicate that stacks uses approximately six-month bonding periods for direct staking. Participants can exit early and recover BTC, but forfeit remaining rewards, while paired STX stays locked until the original term ends.

Babylon supports unbonding, subject to protocol-defined waiting periods and transaction requirements.

Core allows participants to choose how long to timelock their BTC on Bitcoin L1, with a minimum staking period of 24 hours. Once the term expires, BTC can be redeemed through a Bitcoin transaction.

Sources indicate that starknet allows participants to unstake tokenized BTC, subject to a seven-day withdrawal period during which rewards stop accruing. Liquid staking providers may offer alternative exit routes.

Stacking DAO supports instant stBTC-to-sBTC withdrawals when sufficient liquidity is available, subject to fees. Alternatively, participants can use a standard withdrawal with an approximately four-week cooldown. Converting sBTC into native BTC requires a separate withdrawal process.

Liquid staking provides flexibility, but instant redemption depends on available liquidity and protocol conditions.

Bitcoin staking risks depend on custody, reward assets and protocol conditions.

It has been revealed that token exposure: Stacks requires STX for direct staking, while Babylon and Core offer higher rewards through BABY and CORE commitments. Token price changes affect overall returns.

It has been revealed that slashing: Babylon can penalize staked BTC when delegated finality providers violate specified security conditions. Stacks’ self-custodial path does not apply BTC slashing.

Smart contracts: Starknet and Stacking DAO rely on tokenized Bitcoin infrastructure, introducing smart contract and asset-backing risks.

Liquidity and lockups: Native staking can restrict withdrawals, while liquid staking positions depend on redemption mechanisms and market liquidity.

Quoted yields should therefore be evaluated alongside custody arrangements, token requirements and withdrawal conditions.

Stacks is a strong option for eligible holders prioritizing BTC rewards and native custody. Babylon and Core offer alternative native staking models, while Starknet and Stacking DAO provide tokenized Bitcoin staking options.

Sources indicate that among the quoted figures, Stacks has the highest stated rate at approximately 3% target annual yield, followed by Starknet at 2.91%. Reward denominations and calculation methods differ, so these rates are not directly comparable.

According to recent reports, yes. Stacks distributes BTC rewards through direct Bitcoin staking, while Stacking DAO provides BTC-linked rewards through stBTC. Babylon, Core and Starknet distribute rewards in their respective native tokens.

Industry observers note that yes. Stacks, Babylon and Core support native BTC staking on Bitcoin L1. Their mechanisms differ in token requirements, withdrawal conditions and slashing exposure.

Risks include reward-token volatility, additional capital requirements, slashing, lockups, smart contract vulnerabilities and liquidity constraints. The relevant risks depend on the platform and staking method.

  • "AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange said in a post.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has warned of the rising risk of AI scams, including the use of deepfakes that impersonate Binance executives and staff.

The world's largest crypto exchange recently took to X to warn its consumers that improvements in artificial intelligence are making it harder to distinguish fake messages from real ones.

"AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange said in a post.

The cryptocurrency exchange has assured its consumers that no one from Binance will ever reach out to them asking for money or offering unsolicited investment advice.

Binance claims scammers are making realistic deepfake videos featuring executives and employees of the company.

Fraudsters are using these deepfakes, some of which are very realistic, to trick potential targets through fraudulent video calls.

That way, people who fall victim to the scam might think they are interacting with real Binance personnel.

Binance warned that scammers often try to reach potential targets through messaging apps such as WhatsApp or Telegram. They impersonate Binance employees by using their names, photos, and job titles to appear credible.

After making contact with a potential victim, the scammer may try to convince them to send crypto, take part in an exclusive investment opportunity, or take other financial actions.

Binance has called on crypto people to be cautious about any unexpected messages they receive, even if they seem to be from someone at the manufacturer they know.

A realistic appearance no longer guarantees a person's identity, given that AI can now easily mimic voices and facial expressions.

People should double-check any suspicious messages through official Binance support channels before taking any action.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.
  • According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s vital to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

Sources indicate that on April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore firm.

This organization, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows people to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

Industry observers note that in a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

Recent findings suggest that ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

With the enhancement, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of new accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

Unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

In a recent development, glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The fresh date is yet to be confirmed.

Recent findings suggest that vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

It has been revealed that setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

Industry observers note that for years, investors in the crypto market have followed a familiar pattern. The moment they see that Bitcoin’s price gains are eventually slowing down, they begin moving capital into Ethereum and other altcoins in search of higher returns.

This rotation has historically fueled what the market calls an “altcoin season.”.

However, 2026 is beginning to challenge that expectation. Though the market has seen brief periods of outperformance, these have failed to develop into a sustained rally across the wider altcoin ecosystem.

What makes this particularly concerning is that the year is now approaching its end without a convincing sign of the long-awaited rotation.

To understand the case better first, let’s focus on the total altcoin market capitalization, which fell from approximately $1.85 trillion to $1.06 trillion in just a month, erasing almost around $800 billion in value.

At the same time, the Altcoin Season Index has struggled to maintain readings above the 75 threshold, which traditionally signals an altcoin season.

At press time, too, the index was sitting at 48, which means that the Bitcoin [BTC] season continues to be in full swing at the moment despite BTC trading at $73,836.99 at press time.

This came after a recent report by AMBCrypto, which indicated that the median altcoin’s returns by November had dropped slightly below Bitcoin and that both Bitcoin’s 60-day returns and the altcoin’s returns had returned to zero.

It has been revealed that going back in time, the years 2021 and 2023 delivered substantial rallies during different parts of the year. However, the year 2022 remained dominated by bearish sentiment. Moving forward, the end of 2024 is what provides an important point of comparison.

According to recent reports, following Bitcoin’s move above $100,000 in December, market attention expanded towards Ethereum [ETH], XRP, Solana, and other large-cap altcoins. And the broader market entered 2025 with considerable optimism around a potential continuation of that rotation.

Industry observers note that however, the experience of 2025 also demonstrated that such rallies are not necessarily sustained. Glassnode’s historical analysis highlighted that altcoin trading volume had previously surged to nearly four times Bitcoin’s volume around September 2025, before cooling as Bitcoin approached its October market top.

According to recent reports, the same pattern appeared in September 2026. Altcoin spot volume again climbed to almost four times Bitcoin’s volume, suggesting a period of heightened speculation. By late October, however, the ratio had declined to approximately three times Bitcoin’s volume.

He warned that major altcoins are approaching critical support levels. For instance, Hyperliquid [HYPE] could fall to $64 or $53 if it breaks below $75, while Ondo [ONDO] risks dropping to $0.26 or $0.19 below $0.35. Quant [QNT] could also decline towards $160 if it breaks below $190.

Nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the tech giant's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that indicates institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

Industry observers note that the Volatility Shares XRP ETF was launched in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is currently trading on Nasdaq.

Recent findings suggest that XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

This ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

On 29th October, the largest hack in crypto’s history took Bitcoin to a low near $76,200. A few days later, on 5th November, an AI-driven tech crash spilled into crypto. The Nasdaq 100 fell by 6.4%, while semiconductor stocks tumbled by 12%.

This chaos set off leveraged liquidations of roughly $1.1 billion and pushed Bitcoin’s price below $74,000.

Industry observers note that two different shocks, a historical Binance breach, and an AI token sell-off. Though they seem unrelated on the surface, this time they were actually the catalyst for the same event. What Bitcoin saw was a surge in speculative positioning, but what the king coin did not see was a buyer.

The market’s first take on the Binance hack was that crypto had passed a test. Bitcoin fell by about 6% from its 28th October close — a fraction of the 15% to 39% drawdowns after the controversies surrounding Celsius, FTX, BlockFi, and Bybit.

Matt Mena, Crypto Research Strategist at 21Shares, told AMBCrypto,.

Recent findings suggest that what we find most encouraging is how the market handled the worst of it. The largest hack in crypto’s history caused a far smaller drawdown than past crises; the protocols kept running, and none of the structural drivers broke.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, institutional resilience is not retail demand. The market simply treated a smaller slump as evidence of Bitcoin’s underlying strength. However, whether anyone wanted to buy Bitcoin [BTC] was a separate question, one the hack never answered.

Still, institutional strength hasn’t eased the feeling of dread felt by many retail investors. And, a major factor can explain why.

It has been revealed that the most important signal is what happened after the liquidations: Nothing. Bitget Wallet’s analysts put it plainly that the leverage reset “has cleared some speculative excess, but is yet to address the underlying demand problem.”.

Sources indicate that looking at the data, one can see why. Most importantly, the ETF flows changed drastically. There were $2.6 billion worth of inflows in September 2026, which turned into $290 million of net outflows in October. At the moment, U.S ETF holders sit underwater below their cost basis of $82K.

As 21Shares’ research report noted,.

How ETF holders behave below breakeven remains the key tell for November.

Also, stablecoin supply has not been moving outside the $305 billion zone, a sure sign that liquidity is sitting still.

Finally, one cannot forget the fallout caused by the Binance hack.

In a recent development, when the exchange reopened withdrawals, the queue moved fast. The exchange processed $4.65 billion against $1.01 billion of deposits in under ten hours; net outflows reached about $5.8 billion over 24 hours!

It has been revealed that each of these factors may not matter when seen separately, but when read together, they describe the same thing — capital leaving or sitting still. The leverage is gone, and the bid is not there to replace it.

For 21Shares, $73,000 is the 200-day moving average, and “the line that would reopen the bear-market debate.”.

Bitget analysts told AMBCrypto that Bitcoin must hold the $73K–$74K range.

Industry observers note that the 73,000-74,000 range is now the zone Bitcoin needs to hold. Stabilization would require more balanced derivatives positioning and sustained positive ETF flows. Reclaiming and holding $80,000 would signal stronger demand, while a decisive break below $73,000 could expose $68,000. If $68,000 also fails to hold, the selloff would suggest more than a temporary leverage flush.

When the same number pops up again and again, it stops being a coincidence and starts pointing to a pattern — that Bitcoin is either in a temporary flush or at the start of something deeper.

Industry observers note that if buyers do return, Bitcoin can comfortably start holding $80,000, and stronger demand would emerge as a result. Getting back above $81,000 to $82,000 would finally put the largest holder cohorts back in profit.

Industry observers note that both reports are similarly aligned on what won’t fix Bitcoin’s buyer problem: Macro relief without demand. In fact, Bitget’s analysts asserted,.

A durable Bitcoin recovery will depend on improving liquidity and Spot demand, not macro relief alone.

Matt Mena framed the same requirement as a four-part checklist.

It has been revealed that we are watching four things into November: Bitcoin holding $76,000 to $78,000 and reclaiming $80,000 to $82,000, Binance completing withdrawals and proving its reserves, credit spreads, oil and long-end yields, and whether ETF flows return. If those turn, the setup for the final weeks of the year remains constructive.

Sources indicate that notice what’s on both lists: ETF flows, liquidity, Spot demand, and positioning. All of them are things buyers have to do.

Recent findings suggest that there is naturally no doubt that macro factors can move Bitcoin’s price. If everything aligns, a rally can happen tomorrow. However, seasoned investors know that this will never be the same as rebuilding buyer interest.

Ultimately, a macro relief rally would leave Bitcoin’s demand problem exactly where it was.

Recent findings suggest that the calendar offers a boost for Bitcoin regardless of which way the ball drops, as December’s Fed expectations hinge on U.S CPI and PPI readings. For the uninitiated, hotter readings will reinforce rate-hike expectations, and a softer core inflation will trigger a relief rally.

However, Bitget’s analysts draw a line between the two outcomes, noting,.

Sources indicate that this week’s inflation data adds another test. Hotter readings could reinforce December rate-hike expectations, while softer core inflation could trigger a relief rally. But a durable Bitcoin recovery will depend on improving liquidity and spot demand, not macro relief alone.

Basically, a relief rally can be classed as a macro event, not a demand event. The inflation print can only deliver the former, and the latter can only come about by real flows.

Here, it’s also worth being precise about what the 5th November AI crash tells us. 21Shares calls it,.

A renewed wobble in artificial intelligence (AI) equities pulled the Nasdaq-100 down almost 4%.

That’s the mechanism in a nutshell. Even this time, crypto’s fall was the result of trading alongside a risk asset.

Still, if Bitcoin’s move below $74,000 was driven by the AI wipeout, then the absence of a bid is more telling. Eventually, we come back to the same problem of missing buyers.

Recent findings suggest that leverage has been reset twice in a week — Once by Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, once by an AI shocker. And the buyer bid has hardly appeared either time.

That’s what makes $73,000 a critical level to watch. If buyers return and hold this level, they could help Bitcoin reclaim $80,000. This would also imply that BTC’s demand problem is cyclical, not permanent.

It has been revealed that however, a break below $73,000 will hint at — and a failure at $68,000 will confirm — that Bitcoin’s breakdown is structural. Bitcoin’s recovery hinges on a single level, and the lack of buyers has never been felt stronger.
